tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact required format, and place it as the last parseable list in the response.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When finalizing the answer for any Tower of Hanoi problem.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including explanatory text after the move list, causing the parser to miss the moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost disk on its peg, first move any smaller disks that sit above it to other pegs before moving the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that has smaller disks on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 while disk 2 is on top of it, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg; moving any other disk violates the rules.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before executing each move in the generated sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 from a peg where disk 2 is on top, causing a source‑top mismatch.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk, check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk; otherwise the placement is illegal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before each move, after confirming the source.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2, which is smaller.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When moving a stack of k disks from one peg to another using the third peg as auxiliary, recursively move k‑1 disks to the auxiliary, move the largest disk, then move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a contiguous stack of disks between pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move three disks directly without recursively handling the top two, leading to an incomplete or illegal sequence.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg currently holds smaller disks that must end up above the larger disk in the final configuration, move those smaller disks elsewhere before moving the larger disk onto the destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the target peg already contains disks that are smaller than the disk you intend to place there.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to place disk 4 onto a peg that currently has disk 2 on top, while the final order requires disk 2 to be above disk 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal‑first descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the goal is to stack all disks on a single peg, always move the largest remaining disk that can be placed onto the goal peg, then fill in the smaller disks above it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During planning for arbitrary start configurations where the final stack is on one peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a smaller disk onto the goal peg before the larger disk that should be below it, causing later illegal placements.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate final configuration after move generation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state to verify that the final configuration matches the goal; if not, revise the sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After generating the full move list, before outputting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Outputting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg because an earlier move was missed.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use the smallest disk as a flexible temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Treat the smallest disk (disk 1) as a universal temporary buffer: move it onto any larger disk or an empty peg to free up larger disks or to hold a spot while larger moves are performed.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need a temporary place to hold a disk while freeing a larger one.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Failing to move disk 1 out of the way before moving disk 3, causing disk 3 to be blocked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid unnecessary back-and-forth moves; keep solution concise
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When planning the move sequence, each move should bring a disk closer to its final position; avoid moving a disk to a peg and then immediately moving it back unless required to free a larger disk, thereby reducing total moves and preventing token‑limit truncation.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During move generation for any Tower of Hanoi problem, especially when the initial configuration is arbitrary and the solution may become long.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 1 from peg A to peg B and later moving the same disk back to peg A without any larger disk having been moved in between.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generation early or forget to output any moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate at least one move; after solving, output the full move list.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model generates a long sequence that exceeds the token budget, causing the output to be cut off.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the move sequence concise, avoid unnecessary moves, and output only the move list without extra commentary.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may select a disk that is blocked by smaller disks on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model does not verify the destination peg's top disk size.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
